lines.text: Maya's bakery just won its biggest order ever: a supermarket wants twelve thousand loaves a month.
The supermarket will pay her forty thousand dollars. Flour and wages cost thirty thousand. That leaves ten thousand in profit.
But the flour and the wages are due now. The supermarket pays in sixty days.
Maya has only twelve thousand in the bank. The moment she pays her bills, she is eighteen thousand short.
So her bank lends her the difference, and the loan is repaid the day the supermarket pays.
Profitable businesses rarely fail from losses. They fail when the cash runs out first.
